\title{\textbf{The paper training corpus, re-extracted with OpenAlex ids}\\[0.3em]\large Proof that the row set is unchanged, and exact id attachment}

\section*{Verdict}
Across 56 year files (1970--2025), the re-extraction reproduces the training corpus \textbf{exactly}: 99,651,350 rows on both sides, the multiset of abstracts is identical in every year, the multiset of full row keys is identical in every year, and every training row receives an id by exact key (0 unmatched). 402,261 rows (0.4037%) belong to duplicate-record groups (identical text and metadata under two or more ids) and are flagged \pth{id\_ambiguous}; the text they were trained on is not in doubt, only which of the duplicate ids to name.
\textbf{No retraining is implied.} The chains consumed the \pth{abstract} column and nothing else; the id is a label attached afterwards to the very same rows. What changes is auditability: which works a checkpoint saw is now a document-level fact with 100\,\% coverage instead of a title-matched estimate.
\section{Why this was needed}
\pth{OpenAlex/Works\_oa.py} built \pth{OpenAlex/Data/work\_\{year\}.parquet}, the corpus behind every paper chain under \pth{Model/} and \pth{Model\_full/}, from the shared dump \pth{/project/jevans/tip/data/openalex/works.parquet} (405 shards, last modified 2024-03-25). Its \pth{READ\_COLS} omitted \pth{id}, so the corpus carries no work id. \pth{SciTech\_PPP/00\_attach\_openalex\_id\_CPU\_Midway.ipynb} recovered ids afterwards by matching normalised title and publication year against the same dump (\pth{work\_by\_year\_with\_id/}), reaching about 90.1% coverage and, as the PPP abstract audit showed, occasionally linking a row to a different work with the same title (a ChemInform digest and its source article; a neural-stem-cell paper linked to a fuel-assembly abstract).
\section{Method}
\textbf{Re-extraction} (\pth{extract\_work\_ids.py}). The same shards in the same sorted order, the same filter (\pth{language == 'en'} and \pth{publication\_year >= 1970} after \pth{pd.to\_numeric}), the same \pth{reconstruct\_abstract} -- loaded from \pth{Works\_oa.py}'s source at run time so it cannot drift -- and the same \pth{abstract.notna()} drop. Only the column list differs: \pth{id} is read, and the nested columns (\pth{concepts}, \pth{mesh}, \pth{grants}, \pth{open\_access}) are not, because they play no part in the key.
\textbf{Why sets and not positions.} \pth{Works\_oa\_parquet.py} produced each \pth{work\_\{year\}.parquet} with \pth{pyarrow.dataset(...).to\_table()} over a Hive partition whose part files carry UUID names, so the row order of the training file is the discovery order of random file names and cannot be reproduced. The proof therefore compares multisets: for each year, the sorted array of 64-bit hashes of the \pth{abstract} column, and the sorted array of hashes of the full key (\pth{title, abstract, publication\_date, type, authors\_count, referenced\_works\_count, concepts\_count}). Equal length and element-wise equality of the sorted arrays means the two files hold the same rows.
\textbf{Attachment} (\pth{verify\_attach\_ids.py}). Each training row is joined to the re-extraction on the full key. When a key occurs $k>1$ times on both sides (duplicate records in OpenAlex: same text, same metadata, different ids) the ids are assigned within the group by position and the rows are flagged \pth{id\_ambiguous}. No row is ever matched by title alone. The output \pth{OpenAlex/Data/work\_by\_year\_with\_id\_exact/work\_\{year\}.parquet} is the training file, in the training file's row order and with all its columns, plus \pth{openalex\_id} and \pth{id\_ambiguous}.

\section{Against the title+year recovery}
Where both methods assign an id (89,539,542 rows) they agree on 89,539,542 and disagree on 0 (0.000% of title-matched ids). The exact method adds an id to 10,111,808 rows the title match left empty; 0 rows have a title-matched id but no exact id.
\section{Consequences}
\begin{itemize}
\item \pth{work\_by\_year\_with\_id\_exact/} supersedes \pth{work\_by\_year\_with\_id/} for every question of the form ``was this work in the training set of checkpoint $t$''. The PPP audit (\pth{Atypicality/Data check/abstract\_consistency\_check.ipynb}) and the revision build (\pth{Atypicality/build\_ppp\_df\_wabstract\_rev.ipynb}) read it through \pth{OA\_WITH\_ID}.
\item The training files themselves are untouched. The chains under \pth{Model/} and \pth{Model\_full/} remain valid as trained.
\item Retraining would be required only if the corpus \emph{text} changed: a different snapshot (e.g.\ the January 2026 \pth{renli\_shared} dump), a different filter, or de-duplication. Attaching ids is not such a change.
\end{itemize}
